name: Apollonius
description: Son of Thraseas, governor of Celosyria and Phenice; told king Seleucus of the money in the Jerusalem treasury, which Heliodorus was sent to seize; still governing under Antiochus Epiphanes, he increased Simon's malice against Onias

points: And when he could not overcome Onias, he got him to Apollonius the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice. He ran to the other nations. They were working together on this temple, and because of one argument he goes to the other nations against Onias, and told them that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money. You cannot make this stuff up.

Onias, seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius as governor of Coelosyria and Phenice did rage and increase Simon's malice, went to the king: not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both public and private. He didn't even go there to accuse Simon. These are the characteristics of Onias III, a great and upstanding elder man.
